title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U_1 = P^1_Q − {0,1,∞} (= M_{0,3}), and U_n → U_1 is the Fermat cover of level n: the affine Fermat curve x^n + y^n = 1 minus the points over 0, 1, ∞. It is Galois over Q̄ with group (Z/n)^2. Let π̂ = π̂_{0,3} = π_1(U_{1,Q̄}), free profinite on two generators. Let M^ = π̂/[π̂,π̂] ≅ Ẑ(1)^2. As a module over Γ_Q × S_3, M^ is Ẑ(1) tensored with the 2-dimensional (reduced permutation) representation of S_3. The S_3 here is the automorphism group of {0,1,∞}.

The previous page introduced the richer extension (372): 1 → π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) → π_1(U_n, S_3) → Γ_Q × S_3 → 1. The middle term is the fundamental group of the stack-quotient of U_n by S_3, with π_1(U_1, S_3) = 𝓜_{0,3}. It also announced a coarser quotient, adapted to the minimal ('abelian') Lie approximation of the section.

This page fixes that quotient. Divide by the normal subgroup π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) ∩ [π̂,π̂].
- The geometric part becomes M^[n] := π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) / (π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) ∩ π̂').
- M^[n] is canonically the image of π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) in π̂^{ab}, which is nM^ (the kernel of M^ → (Z/n)^2).
- So E_n := π_1(U_n, S_3)^~ is an extension of Γ_Q × S_3 by nM^.

Diagram (373) compares E_n with 'model' extensions G^~_{ρ,σ}[n] and G^~_{ρ,σ} of Ẑ^* × S_3 by M^[n] and by M^. The comparison goes along χ × id, where χ is the cyclotomic character.
- The point: on the abelianized level, Γ_Q acts on M^ only through χ, because M^ is a sum of Ẑ(1)'s.
- So the arithmetic extension is pulled back from a purely 'algebraic' (Lie-type) object G^~_{ρ,σ} ≅ (Ẑ^* × S_3)·M^, a semidirect product.

He then gives a recipe building all the (373) for variable n from the n = 1 case (374), where E_1 = 𝓜_{0,3}/[π̂,π̂]. One chooses an S_3-equivariant splitting of E_1, i.e. of G^~. The text first claims such a splitting is unique up to M^-conjugacy. A later marginal correction replaces this with a set of canonical splittings, in bijection (up to conjugacy) with a group S_3 × Z/2, referring back to section 12°.

The distinguished splitting comes from a 'generic point' of U_∞ = lim U_n lying over the tangential base point J⃗ (presumably 01⃗). This works because the Fermat tower has a compatible system of Q-rational tangential points over 01⃗. The next page concludes:
- E_1 ≅ (Γ_Q × S_3)·M^, a semidirect product.
- E_n = (Γ_Q × S_3)·(nM^).
- A Q-rational point x_n of U_n gives a splitting of the quotient extension E_n^! = Γ_Q·(nM^).

Thus rational points on Fermat curves are encoded as sections of (abelianized) arithmetic fundamental group extensions. This is a section-conjecture-style, 'Lie approximation' framing of the Fermat tower.
errors: The first-written claim that an S_3-equivariant splitting is unique up to conjugation by M^ is doubtful, as Grothendieck himself seems to realize. The obstruction lives in H^1(Ẑ^* × S_3, M^) with M^ = Ẑ(1) ⊗ (2-dimensional rep). Since -1 ∈ Ẑ^* acts by -1, this group is killed by 2, but 2-torsion (e.g. from H^1(Z_2^*, Z_2(1))) need not vanish. The marginal addition introducing a set of canonical splittings indexed by S_3 × Z/2 corrects this.
Notational looseness: 'l'intersection de M_{0,3} dans le groupe des [π̂,π̂]' should read the intersection of π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) with [π̂_{0,3}, π̂_{0,3}].

ideas.what: Quotienting π_1 of the Fermat tower (with its S_3 symmetry, over Q) by π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) ∩ π̂', giving extensions E_n of Γ_Q × S_3 by nM^ ≅ nẐ(1)^2. These are pulled back via the cyclotomic character from 'Lie-model' extensions over Ẑ^* × S_3.
ideas.modern_name: Abelian / metabelian quotients of the Galois action on π_1 of P^1−{0,1,∞} and of Fermat curves; Galois action through the cyclotomic character on H_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985-86, 'Profinite braid groups, Galois representations and complex multiplications'); Anderson (hyperadelic gamma); Deligne (1989)
ideas.where_published: Only allusions in Esquisse d'un programme / letter to Faltings; La Longue Marche notes unpublished

ideas.what: Use of S_3-equivariant (stacky) fundamental group π_1(U_n, S_3) and S_3-equivariant splittings, with the canonical splittings indexed by S_3 × Z/2
ideas.modern_name: π_1 of M_{0,[3]}-type stacks; S_3-orbit of tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura (equivariant/S_3 symmetry of GT relations); Drinfeld
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses M_{0,4}, M_{1,1} with symmetry, not this specific construction

ideas.what: Compatible tangential base point over 01⃗ in the whole Fermat tower U_∞, giving a canonical splitting of each E_n as a semidirect product (Γ_Q × S_3)·nM^
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points and their lifts in towers

ideas.what: A rational point of U_n gives a splitting of Γ_Q·(nM^); rational points of Fermat curves viewed as sections of abelianized arithmetic π_1 extensions
ideas.modern_name: Section conjecture / Kummer-map approach to Fermat curves (abelian level, essentially Kummer classes of x^n, y^n)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (section conjecture, 1983 letter to Faltings); Kim's nonabelian Chabauty is a later analogue

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the Fermat tower, with its full S_3 symmetry and over Q, as a tower of extensions E_n of Γ_Q × S_3 obtained from the minimal (abelian) Lie approximation of 𝓜_{0,3}. Rational Fermat points then become sections. This explicitly ties his 'Lie approximation' program for Galois–Teichmüller to Fermat curves, close in spirit to Ihara's contemporaneous Fermat-tower work. At this abelian level, however, the content is essentially Kummer theory.
missed.quote: Voici une façon de construire "algébriquement" les diagrammes (373) (pour n variable) à partir des diagrammes (374)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's independent pursuit of the Ihara-style Fermat-tower / Galois approach, with S_3-equivariance built in. Of historical rather than technical interest.

missed.claim: The precise set of canonical S_3-equivariant splittings 'correspondant ... au groupe S_3×Z/2' is only sketched in a marginal note and not worked out on this page.
missed.quote: On a un ensemble de scindages canoniques correspondant bien à conjugaison près au groupe S_3×Z/2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It concerns the 2-primary ambiguity of equivariant tangential splittings, which is likely understood implicitly in the literature on tangential base points.

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but fairly routine abelian-level construction relating the Fermat tower to the cyclotomic-character model extension. The ideas parallel Ihara and Anderson's published work; only the S_3-equivariant stack framing and the S_3×Z/2 remark are mildly distinctive.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'π_1(U_n, Q̄), savoir l'intersection de [celui-ci] avec le groupe des commutateurs [π̂_{0,3}, π̂_{0,3}]'. The subgroup intended is π_1(U_{n,Q̄}) ∩ [π̂,π̂], not literally M_{0,3}.
The middle term of the first row of (373) is π_1(U_n, S_3)^~ with overbrace E_n (a struck-out earlier version lies beneath).

The marginal note likely reads: 'On a un ensemble de scindages canoniques correspondant bijectivement (à conjugaison près) au groupe S_3 × Z/2 ... à ceux de l'ext. ... (12°), i.e. ... chacun de ces scindages canoniques ...'. The '(12)' is probably a reference to section 12°.
'On choisit un S_3-[M^-]scindage de la première, i.e. un scindage de la seconde': the M^ is a superscript insertion.
